backlog.title: Core Package v1.0 Spec Compliance
backlog.description: Bring @formality-ui/core to full structural and API-surface compliance with PRD §1.3.1 (package structure) and §1.3.2 (module → key-export table). subtasks.title: Create config/ordering.ts and move ordering functions
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: Per plan/005_8f88e0ec4482/architecture/gap_analysis.md gap G1, the ordering functions sortFieldsByOrder, getUnusedFields, and getOrderedUnusedFields currently live in packages/core/src/labels/resolve.ts (lines ~180-213). PRD §1.3.1 specifies they should be in config/ordering.ts. They are exported from labels/index.ts and the root index.ts barrel under 'Labels & Ordering'. The sole consumer is packages/react/src/components/UnusedFields.tsx which imports from the root @formality-ui/core barrel.
2. INPUT: The existing functions in packages/core/src/labels/resolve.ts — sortFieldsByOrder(fieldNames: string[], fieldConfigs: Record<string, FieldConfig>): string[] (line ~180), getUnusedFields(declaredFieldNames: string[], config: Record<string, unknown>): string[] (line ~198), getOrderedUnusedFields(declaredFieldNames: string[], config: FormFieldsConfig): string[] (line ~213). These use the FieldConfig.order property (PRD §15.14.1.2).
3. LOGIC: Create packages/core/src/config/ordering.ts. Move the three ordering function implementations (including their imports of FieldConfig/FormFieldsConfig types) from labels/resolve.ts to config/ordering.ts. In labels/resolve.ts, replace the implementations with re-exports from '../config/ordering' to maintain backwards compatibility for any code importing from labels/. Add ordering exports to packages/core/src/config/index.ts barrel. The root index.ts already exports them — verify the re-export chain still resolves (index.ts → labels/index.ts → labels/resolve.ts re-export → config/ordering.ts). Mock: none needed — pure functions with no external deps.
4. OUTPUT: config/ordering.ts exports sortFieldsByOrder, getUnusedFields, getOrderedUnusedFields. config/index.ts barrel includes them. labels/index.ts re-exports them (backwards compat). All existing tests (labels.test.ts) and consumers (UnusedFields.tsx) still pass.

milestones.title: API Surface Compliance
milestones.description: Add the PRD §1.3.2 headline named exports that are currently absent: validate(value, rules, validators, formValues) and mergeConfigs(provider, form, field). tasks.title: Add validate() named export to validation/validate.ts
tasks.description: PRD §1.3.2 lists validate(value, rules, validators, formValues) as the headline export of the validation/validate module. Currently core exports runValidator, runValidatorSync, composeValidators instead. Add a validate() wrapper that composes these.

subtasks.title: Implement validate() wrapper over existing validator functions
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: Per gap_analysis.md G2, no function named 'validate' exists in core. The validation module (packages/core/src/validation/validate.ts) exports runValidator (runs a single ValidatorSpec against a value), runValidatorSync (synchronous variant), isValid, and composeValidators (runs an array of validators sequentially). PRD §10.9.2-9.3 specifies the ValidatorSpec type (string | ValidatorFunction | array) and ValidationResult return values (true/undefined = valid, false/string/object = invalid). The resolveErrorMessage function in validation/messages.ts resolves error messages from ValidationResult.
2. INPUT: The existing functions in validation/validate.ts: runValidator(validator: ValidatorSpec, value: unknown, formValues?: Record<string, unknown>, validators?: ValidatorsConfig, errorMessages?: ErrorMessagesConfig) and composeValidators. Also the types from types/validation.ts: ValidatorSpec, ValidationResult, ValidatorsConfig, ErrorMessagesConfig.
3. LOGIC: Implement validate(value: unknown, rules: ValidatorSpec, validators?: ValidatorsConfig, formValues?: Record<string, unknown>): Promise<ValidationResult | undefined> as a thin wrapper that delegates to runValidator/composeValidators. It should: (a) resolve named validators from the validators registry if rules is a string, (b) run the validator(s), (c) return the ValidationResult (the caller resolves error messages via resolveErrorMessage). Follow PRD §9.1 layer order: rules → field validator → type validator (but validate() covers the rules layer only; the field/type layers are handled by Field's Controller rules.validate). Export from validation/index.ts and the root index.ts barrel. Mock: none — pure functions.
4. OUTPUT: validate() exported from @formality-ui/core. New unit tests in validation.test.ts covering: named validator, inline function, async validator, array of validators, valid/invalid return values. Existing 1003 tests unaffected.
5. DOCS: [Mode A] Add JSDoc to validate() explaining it is the PRD §1.3.2 headline export and how it relates to runValidator/composeValidators. This is a new public API export.

tasks.title: Add mergeConfigs() named export to config/merge.ts
tasks.description: PRD §1.3.2 lists mergeConfigs(provider, form, field) as the headline export of the config/merge module. Currently core exports deepMerge, mergeInputConfigs, resolveInputConfig, mergeFieldProps instead. Add a mergeConfigs() wrapper.

subtasks.title: Implement mergeConfigs() wrapper over existing merge functions
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: Per gap_analysis.md G3, no function named 'mergeConfigs' exists. The config/merge module (packages/core/src/config/merge.ts) exports: deepMerge (generic deep merge), mergeInputConfigs (merges provider/form/field InputConfig overrides), resolveInputConfig (resolves the final InputConfig for a field type), mergeStaticProps (ordered spread merge of 8+ prop layers), mergeFieldProps (the full 8-layer merge used by Field component, PRD §5.3.2/§6.1). createConfigContext builds a ConfigContextValue. PRD §6.1 defines the 8-layer priority order.
2. INPUT: The existing functions in config/merge.ts and the types from types/config.ts: InputConfig, FieldConfig, FormalityProviderConfig, FormConfig.
3. LOGIC: Implement mergeConfigs(provider: FormalityProviderConfig, form: FormConfig, field?: FieldConfig): { inputConfig: InputConfig; fieldConfig: FieldConfig } — a high-level wrapper that: (a) merges input type configs via resolveInputConfig using provider.inputs and form.inputs, (b) merges field-level config via mergeFieldProps layers (provider defaultFieldProps → form defaultFieldProps → field config.props). This is a convenience wrapper for the common 3-source merge; the granular functions remain available for advanced use. Export from config/index.ts and root index.ts. Mock: none — pure functions.
4. OUTPUT: mergeConfigs() exported from @formality-ui/core. New unit tests in config.test.ts covering: provider-only, provider+form, provider+form+field, override priority. Existing tests unaffected.
5. DOCS: [Mode A] Add JSDoc to mergeConfigs() explaining it is the PRD §1.3.2 headline export and how it relates to resolveInputConfig/mergeFieldProps. New public API export.

backlog.title: React Package v1.0 Spec Compliance
backlog.description: Bring @formality-ui/react to full module-contract compliance with PRD §1.3.3 (hook table) and §20.7 (overlay docs). The react package is fully functional (all features implemented, 1003 tests), but has two structural/hygiene gaps: the useField hook (PRD §1.3.3) is implemented inline in Field.tsx rather than as a separate hook, and useFieldDisabledState is orphaned dead code.

milestones.title: Hook Architecture Reconciliation
milestones.description: Extract the useField hook from Field.tsx (PRD §1.3.3 requires it as a distinct module) and remove the orphaned useFieldDisabledState hook.

tasks.title: Extract useField hook from Field.tsx
tasks.description: PRD §1.3.3 specifies a hooks/useField module for RHF Controller integration. Currently this logic (~270 lines) is inline in Field.tsx's Controller render block. Extract it into a useField hook that Field delegates to, improving testability and module reusability.

subtasks.title: Design useField hook interface and type contract
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: Per gap_analysis.md G6, the useField hook functionality is in Field.tsx lines ~430-702 (Controller render block). This includes: parse/format pipeline (PRD §5.3.5), change handler (§5.3.6), validation integration (§5.3.7), forwardRef delivery (§20.1 at line 605), and template rendering (§5.3.8). The hook uses: Controller and useWatch from react-hook-form; parse/format/runValidator/resolveErrorMessage/mergeFieldProps from core; useFormContext/useConfigContext/useGroupContext for context; useConditions/usePropsEvaluation/useInferredInputs/useSubscriptions for hooks. PRD §1.3.3 says useField uses transform/pipeline and validation/validate.
2. INPUT: The existing Field.tsx component (702 lines). The hooks it currently composes: useConditions (condition evaluation), usePropsEvaluation (selectProps evaluation), useInferredInputs (dependency inference), useSubscriptions (subscription management). The context hooks: useFormContext, useConfigContext, useGroupContext.
3. LOGIC: Design the useField hook's input/output contract WITHOUT extracting yet. Define a UseFieldParams interface (name, type, disabled prop, hidden, shouldRegister, rest props, children) and a UseFieldReturn interface (fieldState: ControllerFieldState, renderedField: ReactNode, fieldProps: Record<string, unknown>, watchers: Record<string, boolean>, formState: UseFormStateReturn). Create the file packages/react/src/hooks/useField.ts with just the type definitions and a stub. This is a DESIGN step — the extraction happens in S2. Mock: RHF Controller (the real Controller is used, but we design the hook so it's testable in isolation).
4. OUTPUT: packages/react/src/hooks/useField.ts with UseFieldParams and UseFieldReturn types defined, exported from the file. No behavioral change yet.
5. DOCS: [Mode A] Add JSDoc to the useField types explaining they implement PRD §1.3.3's useField module contract.

subtasks.title: Extract Controller integration logic into useField hook
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: The Controller render block in Field.tsx (~lines 430-702) contains the core field logic. Key elements: (a) handleChange callback (Field.tsx ~line 540) that parses value via core parse(), calls controller.field.onChange, notifies via changeField, triggers validation if debounce===false; (b) the Controller render function that merges props via mergeFieldProps (8-layer priority), delivers forwardRef: field.ref (line 605, PRD §20.1), resolves template, handles component vs host-element paths (§20.3/§20.4 forwardRef translation), and supports children render-prop. The disabled state resolution is inline (Field.tsx ~329-362) using useConditions result + groupContext. Condition setValue application is via useEffect (Field.tsx ~259-310) using refs for methods.setValue/getValues to prevent infinite loops (PRD §7.1.1).
2. INPUT: The UseFieldParams/UseFieldReturn types from P2.M1.T1.S1. The existing inline logic in Field.tsx. The hooks Field already composes (useConditions, usePropsEvaluation, useInferredInputs, useSubscriptions).
3. LOGIC: Move the Controller integration, handleChange, parse/format pipeline, validation wiring, props merge, template resolution, forwardRef delivery, and condition setValue effect from Field.tsx into useField.ts. Field.tsx becomes a thin wrapper that: (a) calls useField(name, type, props), (b) handles registration (registerField/unregisterField via useEffect), (c) renders the returned renderedField or children render-prop. The hook calls useFormContext/useConfigContext/useGroupContext internally. CRITICAL: preserve the exact forwardRef delivery (§20.1/§20.4) — forwardRef: field.ref as top-level prop for components, translate to ref for host elements. CRITICAL: preserve the setValue effect's ref pattern (PRD §7.1.1) to prevent infinite loops. Mock: RHF Controller (the real Controller is used; no mocking needed since tests render through Field/Form).
4. OUTPUT: packages/react/src/hooks/useField.ts fully implemented. Field.tsx refactored to delegate to useField. All existing Field tests (Field.test.tsx, Field.forwardRef.test.tsx, FieldForwardRef.acceptance.test.tsx, Field.subscriptionStability.test.tsx) pass without modification. Export useField from index.ts.
5. DOCS: [Mode A] Add JSDoc to useField explaining it owns the RHF Controller integration per PRD §1.3.3. Note the forwardRef delivery contract (§20). This is a new public export.

The full test suite includes: Field.test.tsx (basic rendering, props merge, conditions), Field.forwardRef.test.tsx + FieldForwardRef.acceptance.test.tsx (§20 ref delivery), Field.subscriptionStability.test.tsx (no re-render churn), render-isolation.test.tsx (render function children don't cause cross-validation), integration/complete-form.test.tsx (end-to-end).
